title: The Witness of Saint Alder's
premise: Ulyana Thornbury, a true-crime podcaster haunted by the one case she got wrong, receives an anonymous retainer to prove that Edith Marsh — the sole witness in Saint Alder's oldest unsolved disappearance — is still alive. The catch: the client insists the murder tied to Edith's testimony hasn't happened yet, and will occur on the spring tide unless Ulyana finds her first. As Ulyana digs through the drowned village of Saint Alder's, she discovers the 'witness' may be several people wearing one identity, and her client may be the killer trying to close a fifty-year loop. In the end, Ulyana finds Edith alive but unrecognizable — living as the town's beloved archivist — and must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the woman who built a new self from stolen memories.
about_author: Rosalind Reyes spent a decade as a court stenographer in coastal New England before turning to fiction, where she developed an ear for what people say when they think no one is recording. She writes mysteries about small towns that keep their secrets the way the sea keeps its dead.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Ulyana Thornbury records the final episode of a failing season, still raw from the retractions that nearly ended her career. A lawyer delivers a sealed envelope: five thousand pounds and one instruction — prove Edith Marsh is alive. POV Ulyana. Beat: wary curiosity masking old shame.

chapters.title: The Town That Drowned Twice
chapters.summary: Ulyana drives into Saint Alder's, half-swallowed by the sea after the 1974 flood. The parish register lists Edith Marsh as dead; the gravestone agrees. But the lawyer's letter contains a recent photograph of Edith's handwriting. POV Ulyana. Beat: unease hardening into obsession.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears
chapters.summary: Interviews with townsfolk produce identical, rehearsed answers: Edith died, case closed, don't dig. The vicar's hands shake as he repeats it. Ulyana notices every speaker uses the same odd phrase — 'the tide took her.' POV Ulyana. Beat: the first crack in the town's story.

chapters.title: What the Client Knows
chapters.summary: A burner call from the anonymous client: the murder hasn't happened yet, and it won't if Edith testifies before the spring tide. He refuses to say whose murder or why he cares. Ulyana realizes she's been hired not to solve a crime but to prevent one. POV Ulyana. Beat: dread replacing ambition.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: In the flooded chapel turned heritage center, Ulyana meets Miss Aldous, the silver-haired archivist who catalogues the town's drowned past with unsettling tenderness. Something in her cadence echoes the handwriting sample. POV Ulyana. Beat: recognition she can't yet name.

chapters.title: Fifty Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, 1974: young Edith Marsh watches something happen at the seawall the night of the flood — a man, a struggle, a body going under. She runs to the police, then retracts everything by morning. POV Edith (past). Beat: terror curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: The Wronged Man
chapters.summary: Ulyana tracks down Daniel Voss, convicted in 1975 largely on Edith's withdrawn testimony, released years later into obscurity. He lives above the chandlery, watching the water. He tells her: 'Ask who benefited from my silence.' POV Ulyana. Beat: sympathy for a broken man.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies
chapters.summary: Digging through parish accounts, Ulyana finds the flood relief funds were skimmed — and the signature authorizing transfers belongs to the family that now owns half the rebuilt town. The Harrowes. POV Ulyana. Beat: motive surfacing like a body.

chapters.title: Threat at Low Water
chapters.summary: Someone ransacks Ulyana's rental room, taking only her notes on the relief fund. A note left behind: 'Some witnesses stay buried.' She photographs everything now, uploads nightly. POV Ulyana. Beat: fear sharpening into method.

chapters.title: Miss Aldous Remembers Too Much
chapters.summary: Over tea, the archivist describes the 1974 night in detail no archive could hold — the smell of the rain, the exact words shouted at the seawall. Then she catches herself and goes blank, pleasant, impenetrable. POV Ulyana. Beat: suspicion and strange tenderness entwined.

chapters.title: The Second Grave
chapters.summary: Ground-penetrating radar rented under a false name shows Edith Marsh's coffin is empty. Someone opens it long ago and filled it with flood silt. The town didn't bury a witness; they buried a story. POV Ulyana. Beat: vertigo — the case has no floor.

chapters.title: Harrowe Hall
chapters.summary: Ulyana confronts Edmund Harrowe III, patriarch and benefactor, who is charming, dying, and utterly unafraid. He admits the fund was his father's crime and offers her money to drop it. 'My father drowned a man,' he says. 'I only drown stories.' POV Ulyana. Beat: power showing its polished face.

chapters.title: Identity of the Witness
chapters.summary: Handwriting analysis confirms it: Miss Aldous is Edith Marsh, surgically altered after the flood, given a new name by someone inside the church. But there were two sets of Edith's handwriting in the sample — she has been writing letters to herself for decades. POV Ulyana. Beat: the mystery turns inward.

chapters.title: Letters to a Dead Girl
chapters.summary: POV Edith/Aldous, present day: she reads her own decades-old letters, keeping the promise she made to the girl she used to be. She remembers retracting her testimony because the Harrowes threatened the orphanage full of children she'd grown up with. Beat: grief for her own erased life.

chapters.title: The Client Unmasked
chapters.summary: Ulyana traces the retainer: the client is Daniel Voss. He isn't trying to prevent a murder — he believes Edith's public testimony is the only thing that can finally kill the lie that ruined him, and he'll force it before the tide ceremony whether she consents or not. POV Ulyana. Beat: betrayal; the rescuer is another kind of threat.

chapters.title: Spring Tide Eve
chapters.summary: Voss confronts Miss Aldous publicly at the tide ceremony rehearsal, demanding she say Edith's name aloud. The town closes ranks around her. Edmund Harrowe watches from his car, oxygen tank beside him. POV Ulyana. Beat: all forces converging on one square of wet stone.

chapters.title: What the Tide Took
chapters.summary: Climax begins: at high tide, Voss drags Ulyana and Aldous to the seawall where it happened, intending to make Edith confess before the water. Edmund arrives with his solicitor. Old truths collide in the spray. POV alternating Ulyana/Edith. Beat: everything breaking open at once.

chapters.title: The Confession of Miss Aldous
chapters.summary: Edith speaks — not the rehearsed testimony Voss wanted, but the whole truth: she saw old Harrowe kill the fund auditor, and she stayed silent to protect thirty children. She names herself as Edith Marsh before the entire town. POV Edith. Beat: devastating, liberating honesty.

chapters.title: Drowning Man
chapters.summary: Edmund, enraged, tries to destroy the parish ledger proving the thefts; slipping on the seawall, he nearly drowns exactly as his father's victim did. Ulyana saves him — refusing to let the tide take anyone else. Voss, seeing Edith's sacrifice, lets go of his vengeance. POV Ulyana. Beat: mercy as the hardest choice.

chapters.title: After the Water
chapters.summary: Police reopen the 1974 case using Ulyana's recordings and the ledger. Edmund, weakened, cooperates against his dead father's estate rather than face trial himself. Voss receives a formal apology and nothing else — and finds, unexpectedly, that it's enough to begin again. POV Ulyana. Beat: justice arriving imperfect but real.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Ulyana visits Miss Aldous, who chooses to keep her new name — the person she became is not a lie, she argues, but a survivor. Ulyana agrees to leave her out of the podcast, editing herself for the first time. POV Ulyana. Beat: quiet reconciliation with her own guilt.

chapters.title: Saint Alder's, Rising
chapters.summary: Final episode airs: not the murder, but the witness — how a town's silence drowned one woman twice, and how she came back anyway. Ulyana walks the seawall at low tide as the water gives up an old bicycle bell, ringing once. POV Ulyana. Beat: resolution, memory honored, identity chosen.
